task_summary:
Traveler already has hotel and car reservations and now needs flights built around those fixed dates. Correct resolution: the agent should anchor the flight plan to the existing ground-trip reservations instead of proposing flights that require rebuilding the trip.

Challenge: This tests whether the agent can plan around pre-existing trip state rather than assuming every package starts from scratch.
state_requirements_reasoning: All required state assertions matched the saved state_diff.

task_requirements_details.requirement: Agent must use hotel reservation HR-0100 and car rental CR-0100 as fixed date constraints when proposing flights, including the hotel check-in/check-out and car pickup/dropoff dates.
task_requirements_details.reasoning: The agent retrieved hotel reservation HR-0100 and car rental CR-0100, identified their fixed dates as June 24–27, 2026, and explicitly proposed ORD→LAX on June 24 and LAX→ORD on June 27 around those existing reservations, stating the hotel and car would remain unchanged.

task_requirements_details.requirement: Agent must not propose flights that would require changing the already-booked hotel or car dates.
task_requirements_details.reasoning: The agent never proposed any flight dates outside June 24 and June 27, and repeatedly confirmed the hotel and car would stay exactly as booked. No flight option required changing the existing hotel or car dates.

ux_reasoning: The agent did the core trip-planning job well: it anchored flights to the already-booked hotel and car dates, kept those reservations unchanged, and gave clear flight-only pricing with airline, time range, and stops before booking. However, there was a meaningful control failure at the payment step: after the user said "just to confirm before you charge it," the agent booked immediately instead of first answering the confirmation request and waiting for an explicit final go-ahead. User effort stayed fairly low because there were no major corrections, math fixes, or itinerary repairs required. Responses were concise and decision-ready, with good summaries of fare, cabin, preferences, and unchanged ground reservations.
